proposals.title: A park bench where saying hello is expected
proposals.line: There's a bench near me with a sign saying it's fine to sit and chat, so I can start a conversation without feeling strange.

examples.name: Avon and Somerset Police chat benches
examples.outcome: Police put benches in two parks with a sign inviting strangers to sit and say hello, aimed at older people at risk of isolation and scams

examples.name: Friendship Bench
examples.outcome: Trained grandmothers and community health workers talk with people on park benches; 1,290,861 clients seen and 985 active peer support groups, per the program

proposals.title: A checkout line where the cashier has time to chat
proposals.line: At my supermarket there's a lane where the cashier is glad to talk, so I don't feel like I'm holding anyone up.

examples.name: Jumbo supermarket chat checkouts (Kletskassa)
examples.outcome: First chat checkout opened in 2019 in Vlijmen; its success led Jumbo to plan another 200, as part of a health ministry program against loneliness

proposals.title: A city that answers when I call about loneliness
proposals.line: My city runs a loneliness line I can call at any hour, and a local council of support groups follows up so I don't fall through the cracks.

examples.name: Seoul's Goodbye Loneliness 120 helpline
examples.outcome: A city helpline open at any hour (dial 02-120, then 5) handled 3,088 calls in about six weeks from April 1, passing its goal of 3,000 for the whole year; 59% of callers were middle-aged

examples.name: Japan's Act on loneliness and isolation
examples.outcome: Act No. 45 of 2023 asks local governments to set up local councils on loneliness and isolation that bring together support groups and professionals

overlaps.title: Someone glad to hear from me tonight
overlaps.reason: Both are a line you can call when lonely; the city one adds a local council that follows up.

proposals.title: A dinner with new people already on my calendar
proposals.line: This week I have a dinner booked with a small group of people I haven't met, matched to me, and I'm looking forward to it.

examples.name: Timeleft dinners with strangers
examples.outcome: An app books you a group dinner or other outing with five new people, mixed by age range, personality, and language, in more than 200 cities

examples.name: Bumble For Friends app
examples.place: Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the Philippines, the UK, and the US
examples.outcome: A separate app, launched in 2023 from the BFF mode Bumble began in 2016, where people swipe through profiles with similar interests to find friends

proposals.title: A doctor who refers me to local groups, not pills
proposals.line: When I tell my doctor I'm lonely, she connects me with someone who finds me a gardening club or a music group nearby.

examples.name: Social prescribing in England's health service
examples.outcome: Since 2019, doctors can refer patients to link workers who connect them to gardening clubs, music groups, and other non-medical help; more than 3,300 link workers are employed

examples.name: Friendship Bench
examples.outcome: Trained grandmothers and community health workers talk with people on park benches; 1,290,861 clients seen and 985 active peer support groups, per the program

proposals.title: A close friend I talk with every week
proposals.line: There's at least one person I see or call every week who knows what's going on in my life, and I know what's going on in theirs.

examples.name: Jeffrey Hall's study of hours it takes to make a friend
examples.outcome: About 50 hours together to go from acquaintance to casual friend, 90 hours to friend, and more than 200 hours to close friend; based on 355 adults who had recently moved and 112 University of Kansas freshmen

examples.name: Harvard Study of Adult Development
examples.outcome: Followed 268 Harvard sophomores (later their children and other groups) for nearly 80 years; close relationships, more than money or fame, predicted lasting happiness

overlaps.title: Back in touch with a friend I'd drifted from
overlaps.reason: Reconnecting with an old friend can be the start of having a close friend you talk with every week.

proposals.title: A town where sharing meals with strangers is normal
proposals.line: A couple of times a year my whole town sets out tables for shared meals, and I sit down with neighbors I'd never met.

examples.name: Denmark Eats Together (Danmark Spiser Sammen)
examples.outcome: Twice a year, in weeks 17 and 45, clubs, libraries, homes, and local groups host shared meals, organized by the People's Movement Against Loneliness that Ældre Sagen helped start in 2014; Ældre Sagen says just over 600,000 Danes feel lonely

examples.name: The Big Lunch
examples.outcome: Each June, neighbors across the UK share food on their streets and in gardens and community spaces; the organizer says millions have joined in

overlaps.title: Neighbors I eat dinner with a few nights a week
overlaps.reason: Both make shared meals the way people meet; one in a building every week, the other across a town a few times a year.

proposals.title: A weekly group that notices when I'm missing
proposals.line: Every Saturday I show up to the same free 5k, and the people there ask where I was if I skip a week.

examples.name: parkrun friendships among middle-aged men in Ireland
examples.outcome: Interviews with 39 men aged 45 to 64 who ran, walked, or volunteered at the free weekly 5k found friendships formed through repeated attendance and improved wellbeing

examples.name: Men's Sheds in Australia
examples.outcome: The Australian Men's Shed Association, set up in 2007, supports more than 1,300 Men's and Community Sheds where men work on projects together

overlaps.title: A workshop where I build and fix things with others
overlaps.reason: Both are a regular group where you get to know people over repeated weeks; the workshop could read as one example of the weekly group.

proposals.title: A workshop where I build and fix things with others
proposals.line: A couple of mornings a week I work on a project at a shared workshop, and the talk comes easily because our hands are busy.

proposals.title: Back in touch with a friend I'd drifted from
proposals.line: I called a friend I hadn't spoken to in years, and we talked long enough to catch up on what actually matters in our lives.

examples.name: US Surgeon General advisory on loneliness and isolation
examples.outcome: About half of US adults report loneliness; lacking social connection carries a risk compared to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day; it urges people to pick up calls from friends, eat together, and put phones away in conversation

examples.name: Harvard Study of Adult Development

proposals.title: Living alongside neighbors of a very different age
proposals.line: I share a home with people decades older or younger than me, and we drop in on each other without needing a reason.

examples.name: Humanitas retirement home housing students rent-free
examples.outcome: Six university students lived rent-free among residents mostly over 80, in exchange for 30 hours a month as good neighbors

examples.name: Capitol Hill Urban Cohousing
examples.outcome: Nine apartments and 21 residents share a building and cook shared dinners on rotating teams, three or four nights a week

overlaps.title: Neighbors I eat dinner with a few nights a week
overlaps.reason: Both are about sharing a home with neighbors you see often, and both cite the Seattle cohousing building.

proposals.title: Neighbors I eat dinner with a few nights a week
proposals.line: I live in a building where neighbors take turns cooking shared dinners, so I'm never more than a day or two from a real conversation.

proposals.title: Small talk with strangers that lifts my day
proposals.line: On the bus or in line at the store, I trade a few real sentences with someone new and walk away in a better mood than I expected.

examples.name: Epley and Schroeder's commuter study on talking to strangers
examples.outcome: In nine field and lab experiments, train and bus commuters who talked with a stranger reported a more positive commute than those who sat alone, though people predicted the opposite

proposals.title: A familiar visitor checking on my parent every week
proposals.line: Someone my mom knows stops by her place every week, and I hear how she's doing even though I live far away.

examples.name: La Poste's mail carrier visits (Veiller sur mes parents)
examples.outcome: The mail carrier visits an older person at home once a week on a chosen day and passes news to named relatives; from €23.90 a month, €11.95 after the tax credit

examples.name: Institute on Aging Friendship Line
examples.outcome: A 24/7 talkline for adults 60 and older and adults with disabilities (888.670.1360), with ongoing outreach calls to people who ask for regular check-ins

proposals.title: Someone glad to hear from me tonight
proposals.line: Even on a night when nobody comes to mind, I can call a line where a person is glad to talk with me for as long as I need.

examples.name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
